# File-type filtering in `ignore`

ripgrep's `--type`/`--type-not`/`--type-add` machinery lives entirely in the
`ignore` crate, in two files: `crates/ignore/src/types.rs` (the logic) and
`crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs` (the shipped type list). This note covers
how definitions are represented, how a `Types` matcher is built, and what to
watch for when editing this area.

## Representation

A single type is a `FileTypeDef { name: String, globs: Vec<String> }`
(`types.rs:145`). The name is the label a user passes to `--type` (`rust`,
`cpp`); the globs are the file-name patterns that recognize it. Nothing here is
compiled yet — a `FileTypeDef` is just strings.

The default list is `DEFAULT_TYPES: &[(&[&str], &[&str])]`
(`default_types.rs`), a static array of `(names, extensions)` pairs, e.g.
`(&["bat", "batch"], &["*.bat"])`. One entry can bind several *aliases* to the
same glob set; `TypesBuilder::add_defaults` (`types.rs:482`) flattens this by
looping over every `name` × `ext` and calling `add(name, ext)`, so `bat` and
`batch` become two independent `FileTypeDef`s that happen to share globs. The
list is kept sorted lexicographically and 79-column-wrapped by convention;
`#[rustfmt::skip]` means rustfmt will not do this for you.

## Building a matcher

`TypesBuilder` (`types.rs:305`) holds `types: HashMap<String, FileTypeDef>` and
an ordered `selections: Vec<Selection<()>>`. Definitions and selections are
distinct: defining a type only makes it *available*; `select`/`negate` decide
what actually filters.

Definitions arrive three ways:

- `add(name, glob)` — appends one glob to the named def, creating it if absent.
  It rejects the reserved name `all` and any name containing a non-alphanumeric
  character (`types.rs:417`), returning `Error::InvalidDefinition`.
- `add_def(def)` — parses the user-facing string form by splitting on `:`
  (`types.rs:442`). Two colons of content mean `{name}:{glob}`; three mean
  `{name}:include:{comma,separated,names}`, which copies the globs of each
  referenced (already-defined) type into the new one. The `include` branch
  checks *all* referenced names exist before copying any glob, so a bad
  reference leaves the builder unchanged (`test_invalid_defs` asserts this
  atomicity).
- `add_defaults()` — bulk-loads `DEFAULT_TYPES`.

`select(name)`/`negate(name)` push `Selection::Select`/`Selection::Negate`
onto the list; the special name `all` expands to a selection per currently
defined type (`types.rs:381`, `:395`). `Selection` (`types.rs:185`) is generic
over its payload so it can carry `()` in the builder and a resolved
`FileTypeDef` in the built matcher.

`build()` (`types.rs:322`) is where strings become a matcher. It walks
`selections` in order; for each, it looks up the definition (missing →
`Error::UnrecognizedFileType`) and compiles every glob with
`GlobBuilder::new(glob).literal_separator(true)` into a single `globset::GlobSet`.
`literal_separator(true)` is important: `*` will not cross `/`, so type globs
match against a file name, not a path. Two side tables are produced:
`glob_to_selection`, mapping each glob's index in the set back to
`(selection index, glob index)`, and `has_selected`, true if any selection is a
`Select`. The result `Types` (`types.rs:164`) owns the `GlobSet`, the resolved
selections, those tables, and an `Arc<Pool<Vec<usize>>>` scratch buffer for
match results.

## Matching

`Types::matched(path, is_dir)` (`types.rs:261`) returns
`Match<Glob>`—`Whitelist`, `Ignore`, or `None`. The rules:

- Directories and an empty glob set short-circuit to `Match::None`; type
  filters never apply to directories.
- Only the file name is matched (`pathutil::file_name`).
- `set.matches_into` collects every matching glob index into the pooled
  buffer. **The last (highest-index) match wins** — precedence is selection
  order, so later `--type`/`--type-not` flags override earlier ones. The
  winning glob's selection decides `Whitelist` (selected) vs `Ignore`
  (negated).
- If nothing matched but at least one type was *selected* (`has_selected`),
  the path is `Ignore(Glob::unmatched())` — selecting a type implicitly
  excludes everything else. With only negations, a non-match is `Match::None`.

`Glob` (`types.rs:110`) reports which `FileTypeDef` produced a match, or
`UnmatchedIgnore` for the implicit-exclusion case. In the wider pipeline
(`dir.rs:399`) a type `Ignore` is final, while a `Whitelist` is held and can
still be overridden by later ignore rules.

## For contributors

- Adding a default type is usually a one-line edit to `DEFAULT_TYPES`; keep it
  sorted and wrapped (rustfmt won't). Aliases are just extra names in the tuple.
- Globs are file-name globs. Because of `literal_separator(true)`, a pattern
  like `src/*.rs` will not behave as a path glob.
- Precedence is *last selection wins*, and `has_selected` flips an unmatched
  path from `None` to `Ignore`; changes to either alter user-visible semantics.
- Definitions are order-independent (a `HashMap`), but `definitions()`
  (`types.rs:367`) clones, sorts globs, then sorts defs by name, so output is
  deterministic — rely on that for tests, not on insertion order.
- Preserve `add_def`'s fail-fast validation; partial application of an
  `include` def is a regression the existing tests guard against.
